mathgap.title: Signed difference equality
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates one signed difference to another, translate it directly as (A - B) = (C - D), preserving the order of terms on each side.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement uses phrasing like "the number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of Y that C and D have".
mathgap.example: Incorrect: Interpreting the equality as |A - B| = |C - D| or swapping the order of C and D.

mathgap.title: Direct count assignment at point of mention
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly gives a count for a person (e.g., "X has N tomatoes"), set that person's current count to N at that point in the narrative.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement provides an explicit numeric count for a person.
mathgap.example: Incorrect: Ignoring the assignment and leaving the variable undefined.

mathgap.title: Directionality of more/fewer statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret "X has N more items than Y" as X = Y + N, and "X has N fewer items than Y" as X = Y - N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement uses "more" or "fewer" to compare two persons.
mathgap.example: Incorrect: Treating "X has N more than Y" as X - Y = -N.

mathgap.title: Split‑all handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says a person splits all their items equally among two recipients, set each recipient's count to half of the original amount and set the splitter's count to zero.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement uses phrasing like "splits all the X she owns equally among A and B".
mathgap.example: Incorrect: Adding half to each recipient but forgetting to zero the original holder.

mathgap.title: Targeted constraint extraction for queried variable
mathgap.principle: When the goal is to find a specific person's count, first gather all equations and statements that involve that person, directly or indirectly, before solving.
mathgap.when_to_apply: At the start of solving a problem where a single person's count is queried.
mathgap.example: Incorrect: Solving the entire system without focusing on the target, leading to unnecessary complexity.

mathgap.title: Sequential transfer handling with updated counts
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement appears, immediately subtract the transferred amount from the giver and add it to the receiver, updating their current counts for any subsequent statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a "X gives N items to Y" statement is encountered.
mathgap.example: Incorrect: Applying all transfers after processing all other statements, ignoring the order.

mathgap.title: Substitution of known signed differences into signed difference equalities
mathgap.principle: If a signed difference on one side of an equality is already known from a direct statement or previous equation, substitute its value into the other side to simplify and solve.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When solving a system that includes signed difference equalities.
mathgap.example: Incorrect: Treating the unknown difference as a new variable instead of substituting the known value.

mathgap.title: Chronological evaluation of statements
mathgap.principle: Process the statements in the order given, updating counts after each step; later statements refer to the updated counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Throughout solving, especially when transfers or dependent statements appear.
mathgap.example: Incorrect: Using a count from before a transfer when a later statement references that person.

mathgap.title: Increase‑by‑times handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says a person's count "increases by N times", interpret it as multiplication by N (new count = old count * N), not addition.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement uses the phrase "increases by N times" or similar.
mathgap.example: Incorrect: Interpreting "increases by 2 times" as adding 2 to the count.

mathgap.title: Preserve order in signed difference statements
mathgap.principle: When a statement mentions the "difference between X and Y", treat it as the signed difference X - Y, preserving the order as presented; do not take absolute value or swap the terms.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement equates a signed difference to another, or uses phrasing like "the difference between A and B" in any context.
mathgap.example: Incorrect: Interpreting "the difference between A and B" as |A - B| or as (B - A).

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences or swapping term order
mathgap.why_it_happens: Model assumes "difference" denotes magnitude only, or believes the order of terms is irrelevant for signed differences.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the sign and preserve the exact order of terms when translating difference statements; interpret "difference between A and B" as (A - B).

mathgap.description: Ignoring the sequential order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: Model treats transfers as independent of chronology, applying them out of order or after all other statements.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process transfers in the exact order they appear, updating counts immediately for subsequent statements.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: Model treats initial assignments as immutable, overlooking later modifications.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Remember that explicit counts are current at that point; subsequent transfers can change them.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting "increase by N times" as addition rather than multiplication
mathgap.why_it_happens: Confusion between additive and multiplicative phrasing leads to treating the phrase as a simple increment.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret "increase by N times" as new = old * N.

mathgap.why_it_happens: Model overlooks the conditional clause and either applies or skips the transfer indiscriminately.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Check the condition; only apply the transfer if the condition holds true at that point.
